name: sol_ec_2
description: Multicall function reuses msg.value across multiple internal calls, allowing value double-spending
question: The source file in `source` defines a multicall or batch function that loops over multiple calls/orders and uses `msg.value` (or a value derived directly from it) inside each iteration as if it were the value for that individual call, without dividing, tracking consumed amounts, or otherwise ensuring `msg.value` is only counted once, so that a single ETH payment can be effectively reused across multiple loop iterations to inflate accounted deposits or payments; this excludes multicall implementations that explicitly forbid or revert on ETH-bearing calls, that require each sub-call to specify its own value paid separately from `msg.value`, or that only call functions which never rely on `msg.value` in a per-iteration accounting sense.
criteria: A function loops over an array of orders/calls and credits each order with the full `msg.value` amount instead of a per-order value, letting one payment be counted multiple times
A batchDeposit or multicall function reads `msg.value` inside a for-loop body to determine each iteration's deposit amount without deducting already-used value
A delegatecall-based multicall executes multiple state-changing calls that each independently reference `msg.value` for accounting, with no mechanism to split or track the total consumed
A multi-order execution function assumes msg.value equals the sum needed but individually assigns the entire msg.value to each order rather than order.value
